pages.title: Multiple Choice Question
pages.content:
What will be the output of this code, if the user enters Chef?

```kotlin
fun main(args : Array) {
    var s : String? = null
    s = readLine()
    print("Your name is: $s")
}
```

practiceProblems.title: Taking user input
practiceProblems.description:
You have already learned that **print** is used to output (print) values. \
Now we will use **readLine()** to get user input.

readLine() is a built-in Kotlin function used for reading input from the user through the standard input (usually the keyboard).\
It reads a line of text that the user enters and returns it as a String. 

However we are taking integer as an input here, so as a readLine() returns string so we have to convert it using **toInt()** function.

```kotlin
val input = readLine()
var a = input!!.toInt()
```

In the above code, the double exclamation mark (`!!`) is called the non-null assertion operator. \
It is used to assert that a variable is not null, and it forces the compiler to treat the expression as non-nullable. \
When you use `!!`, you are telling the compiler that you are certain that the variable is not null, and you want to proceed with the assumption that it has a valid value.

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Declare an integer variable $a$
- Try taking a number from the console and assign it to $a$
- Output $a$ to the console

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Declare an integer variable $a$
- Try taking a number from the console and assign it to $a$
- Output $a$ to the console
constraints:
- $1 \leq T \leq 100$
- $1 \leq N \leq 100$
- $1 \leq M \leq N\cdot(N-1)/2$
- $1 \leq u_i, v_i \leq N$
- $u_i \neq v_i$ for each $1 \leq i \leq M$.
- The sum of $N$ over all test cases won't exceed $100$.
practiceProblems.inputFormat:
- The first line of input will contain a single integer $T$, denoting the number of test cases.
- Each test case consists of multiple lines of input.
    - The first line of each test case contains two space-separated integers $N$ and $M$ — the number of vertices and edges of the graph, respectively.
    - The next $M$ lines describe the edges. The $i$-th of these $M$ lines contains two space-separated integers $u_i$ and $v_i$, denoting an edge between $u_i$ and $v_i$.
practiceProblems.outputFormat: For each test case, output on a new line the number of good subgraphs of $G$, modulo $10^9 + 7$.

practiceProblems.title: Hello user
practiceProblems.description:
Write a program which does the following
- Declare a string variable $x$
- Accept a text user input - the name of the user - and store it in the variable $x$
- Output and print to the console "Hello" before the user defined name. \
Remember to add a space between "Hello" and $x$

practiceProblems.title: Find the Area of any rectangle
practiceProblems.description:
Let us revisit our favourite rectangle and its area problem

Write a program which does the following
- Declare 2 integer variables $length$ and $width$
- In this problem - accept 2 user defined inputs from the console and initialise these values $length$ and $width$
- Create another integer variable $area$ - compute the area of the rectangle and store it as $area$
- Output $area$ to the console
